title: Benchmark matrix runner (H100/L40S) + result persistence tags (profile_version, git sha)
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context: As part of the Hardware tuning profiles pack work, we need a reproducible benchmark matrix runner that can be invoked in benchmark-lab CI and produces artifacts that are directly comparable across runtime/profile changes.

This PR adds a first-class matrix runner for the H100 and L40S suites and standardizes result persistence so every run is tagged with: (a) runtime git sha, and (b) profile_version (when enabled), plus SKU + driver/CUDA identifiers.

Key changes: - Add matrix definitions for H100 + L40S (models, prompt/response distributions, concurrency buckets). - Add a CLI runner that expands the matrix, dispatches runs, and writes results + metadata manifest. - Persist results to the benchmark artifact store with stable paths and required tags: runtime_git_sha, profile_version, sku, driver, cuda, region, model, workload_bucket. - Add schema validation + preflight checks to fail fast on missing tags to prevent "orphan" results that can’t be compared. - Add GitHub Actions job wiring to run a small subset (smoke) on PRs and the full matrix on scheduled/nightly runs.

Non-goals: This does not add B200 coverage yet (separate PR once early fleet stabilizes). It also doesn’t change runtime behavior; it just improves measurement + attribution.

Rollout/usage: - Local: `benchlab matrix run --suite h100 --runtime-sha <sha> --profile-version 1.0.0` - CI nightly uses the current runtime main SHA and pins the profile_version from the runtime build metadata.

Risk: Low/medium. Biggest risk is tag cardinality / storage path explosion; mitigated by a capped tag set and a manifest file we can query instead of filename parsing.

Testing: unit tests for matrix expansion + tag enforcement; integration test uses a stub runner and verifies artifacts + manifest content.
commits: benchlab/matrix: add H100 + L40S suite definitions and workload buckets
benchlab/cli: add `matrix run` command + expansion logic
results: write manifest.json with required tags and environment capture
storage: persist results with stable prefix and tag enforcement
ci: add PR smoke + nightly full-matrix workflows
tests: unit + integration coverage for tagging and persistence paths
changed_files: suites/l40s_matrix.yaml (new) — L40S-specific concurrency caps + stability notes
results/manifest.py (new) — required tag schema and writer
results/persist.py — stable artifact path + metadata tags
conversation:
Claire Dubois (review): The matrix buckets look good, but I’m worried we’re going to lose comparability if profile_version is optional. Can we enforce a sentinel value when the runtime isn’t profile-pack aware? Also please document the exact prompt/response distributions used in each bucket so we can map back to the Confluence acceptance thresholds.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Agree. I added `profile_version=none` as a required field when the runtime doesn’t export it, and updated README + manifest schema so it’s always present. Also added per-bucket distribution notes in the suite YAML (p10/p50/p90 prompt and decode lengths) so we can link to acceptance thresholds.

Marcus Reed (review): Two asks: (1) Make sure we capture queueing vs compute timing separately if available; otherwise store the raw trace path in the manifest. (2) Can we include a deterministic `run_id` to correlate across dashboards?

Rina Kobayashi (author): (1) We now persist `trace_uri` when provided by the runner; otherwise it’s null but the field exists. (2) Added `run_id` as `benchlab_<timestamp>_<shortsha>_<suite>` and include it as a tag + manifest field.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI: PR smoke should not upload large artifacts for forks. Please gate uploads and ensure secrets aren’t required for basic test execution.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated workflow: for PRs from forks we run the smoke subset but skip artifact uploads (no secrets). Internal PRs upload to the artifact store.

Allison Grant (review): Tag names: please align with observability-pack naming. Can we use `profile_id` vs `profile_version`? Also watch cardinality on `model` tag.

Omar El-Sayed (review): For runtime-side alignment, we’ve standardized on `profile_version` for the pack artifact and `profile_id` for the active per-SKU profile inside the pack. This PR should store both if available, but at minimum must store profile_version.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated: manifest supports both `profile_version` (required) and `profile_id` (optional). Also `model` is stored in the manifest but not emitted as a storage path component; we keep storage prefixes bounded to avoid path explosion.

Final approvals: Claire + Marcus + Sahana approved after changes. Merged with squash.
release_notes: Benchmark-lab now supports running the H100/L40S benchmark matrix via `benchlab matrix run` and persists results with required tags including runtime_git_sha and profile_version for reliable perf comparisons across profile pack rollouts.
